subject: New York this week: the Marble Hill shooting, remote deportation judges, and a retirement that ended a discipline case
intro: Seven emails over about three weeks. Each one covers a single stage of a New York criminal case, from the arrest to sealing the record, and gives you the exact questions to ask the lawyer at that stage. It starts the day you sign up.

items.title: ICE Supervisor at Center of NYC Shooting Named in Multiple Lawsuits Alleging Violent, Illegal Arrests
items.summary: Brenden Cuni, the ICE supervisor seen holding an assault rifle at the Marble Hill shooting scene, has been named in earlier lawsuits accusing him of beating and tasing immigrants during arrests. DHS has not said which agent fired.

items.title: In Call With Mamdani, White House Demanded NYPD Arrest Immigrant Shot by ICE Agents
items.summary: In calls with Mayor Mamdani, the Department of Homeland Security wanted the NYPD to arrest the man ICE shot in Marble Hill. City officials refused, saying the NYPD can't arrest someone without a warrant, according to a source familiar with the calls.

items.title: ‘Normalize Bad Tactics’: ICE Keeps Shooting at People in Cars
items.summary: The Marble Hill shooting is one of more than 20 by immigration agents in Trump's second term, by The Marshall Project's count, and most of the people shot were in cars. The piece asks use-of-force experts about firing at moving vehicles.

items.title: NYC Immigrants' Newest Obstacle? Remote 'Deportation Judges'
items.summary: Over three days in September, New York Focus watched 23 immigration judges at 26 Federal Plaza. Ten of them, almost all new hires, appeared by video instead of in the courtroom.

items.title: NYPD Blames ‘Human Error’ After Officer in Win Rozario Shooting Is Allowed to Retire
items.summary: An officer facing misconduct charges in the 2024 death of Win Rozario, 19, will avoid a disciplinary trial because the NYPD didn't tell the Civilian Complaint Review Board he had filed to retire. Commissioner Tisch acknowledged the mistake.

ours.title: DHS Says Its Officers Feared for Their Lives in Marble Hill. New York's Parole Board Has to Put a Danger Finding in Writing.
